subject: Fallback ban + forced model lock — playbook & risk checklist
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@pharmaco.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Holloway <tom.holloway@pharmaco.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: no-fallback + model pin for PHC pilot

Hi Dev —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. For the pilot with our internal clinical review team we need a hard guarantee: all inference for PHC data must remain in us-west-2 and should not fall back to any other variant or region. We also need to pin the model to the quantized 8-bit variant you showed (Q8-small-v2) for parity with our validation set.

We understand this is an exception to typical routing/fallback behavior; please advise what you need from our side (paperwork, amended SLA) and how Redwood plans to operationalize this for a 6-week pilot.

Emily
Emily Park
Senior Product Manager — Pharmaco Health
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@pharmaco.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: no-fallback + model pin for PHC pilot

Folks — looping you in. Pharmaco is requesting a strict region lock (us-west-2 only) and a forced model selection (Q8-small-v2) with no fallback allowed for a six-week pilot. They want concrete operational controls and an SLA amendment.

Ask: can we run this safely? Outline of concerns I want us to cover:
- Can Dedicated/private routing honor a hard no-fallback policy? (Marcus)
- What are the availability and latency SLO implications if we do not allow fallback?
- Any security/compliance gating (Karthik) — e.g., logs, KV cache handling, KMS keys?
- Product/console changes required for pinning and visibility to the customer (Lauren)

I attached the draft SLA and their internal statement of intent.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@pharmaco.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: no-fallback + model pin for PHC pilot

Quick operational readout:
- We can implement a hard region lock in Dedicated / Private by using a routing policy tied to the customer's tenant and an isolation tag — yes. For hosted customers this is trickier and higher risk.
- No-fallback means single-zone/regional risk: if the pool goes down we have to either (a) return 503s or (b) fail-over to an approved degraded variant in-region. The customer explicitly forbids fallback; if they insist on 503s we need an SLA carve-out and a clearly written incident window process.
- Pinning to Q8-small-v2 is supported, but we must validate that the quantized kernel set for our target GPU fleet is available in us-west-2. On one of our newer instances the kernel path is still experimental — I'll run a compatibility test (expected 24–48h).
- Operational actions: reserve a dedicated pool in us-west-2, pre-warm KV caches with a subset of prompt prefixes, and set up a strict rollout lock so automatic fallback pipelines are disabled. This requires a temporary override in routing-config and an ops playbook for incidents.

I'll post the compatibility test results and a short ops SOP.

Marcus Lin
Platform Operations Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@pharmaco.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: no-fallback + model pin for PHC pilot

Product concerns / items we must address before approving:
1) Visibility: the customer needs live routing transparency (which model variant is serving each request). We need to expose per-request model id and region in the Console and via token-level tracing. Quick UI/telemetry change required — ETA 2 weeks for a push to staging.
2) Rollout safety: forced model locks bypass canary rollout protections. We should require a short manual verification step (smoke test suite) that the pinned variant passes their eval set before enabling the lock.
3) Billing and quotas: determine how billing is measured if in-region resources are reserved and unused. Finance must sign off on a reservation credit for the pilot.
4) Contractual language: no-fallback + single-region increases our operational exposure; Legal/Finance will need an indemnity clause and explicit incident SLAs.

If we can get Marcus's compatibility sign-off and Karthik's security checklist, Product can scope the minimal telemetry change and the manual verification flow.

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP Product — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@pharmaco.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: no-fallback + model pin for PHC pilot

Security/compliance checklist (high level):
- Data residency: ensure logs (request/response metadata, KV cache keys, traces) are stored in customer-controlled buckets in us-west-2. We need to create a KMS key scoped to the tenant and verify cross-region replication is disabled.
- Auditability: enable enhanced audit logging for the pilot and share the log sink (read-only) with Pharmaco for the pilot period.
- Cryptographic keys: confirm HSM/KMS access patterns for the pinned variant do not fall back to key material in other regions.
- SOC2/ISO: Legal will need an addendum that references our audit controls; compliance may require a 2-week notice before pilot start for paperwork.

I recommend a short compliance intake form (I attached a template) and a 10-business-day lead time to provision keys and validated logging.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@pharmaco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: no-fallback + model pin for PHC pilot

Emily — thanks for patience. Summary and proposed next steps:

Summary of internal constraints:
- We can support a hard us-west-2 region lock for Dedicated/private with the caveat that we will return 503s if the dedicated pool becomes unhealthy and we will not auto-fallback. Marcus is validating kernel compatibility for Q8-small-v2 in us-west-2 (results in 24–48h).
- Security needs 10 business days to provision tenant-scoped KMS and set audit sinks.
- Product will add per-request model and region tracing to the Console (staging ETA ~2 weeks) and requires a manual smoke verification before lock activation.
- Legal/Finance will need SLA addendum and reservation credit language; I'll loop in Contracts after Marcus's compatibility pass.

Proposed operational playbook (pilot flow):
1) Pharmaco signs SLA addendum (we'll send a redline template).
2) We provision a dedicated pool in us-west-2 and tenant KMS + audit sinks (10 business days).
3) Marcus runs kernel compatibility tests and we run the Pharmaco smoke suite.
4) Product enables tracing and we run verification in staging.
5) We enable the no-fallback lock for the pilot window and share the incident runbook with Pharmaco.

Can you confirm pilot target start date range? If Pharmaco can start the paperwork this week, we can aim for a March 15 start.

I attached the SLA draft and the exception intake form.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
